I scoped the Wash Bouldres last year with Chooch and knew I wanted to get back here. Thank goodness I had fellow single boy, the one and only Mr. Dirk Irector to join me on this lovely fitness day! This climb has cleaned up a ton since I looked at it last year and the features are great and the line is inspiring.  A little like the "Hail Mary (way lake)" of Joes. That last reach is just far enough to turn caterpillars into butterflies. Ran into a super rad group of guys here. We were well met. Ka.
Hmmm... Human Music, I like it!

What a wild ride. I think me n scott are straight beat off at this point. Im a mantle machine and this tough lip encounter was indeed a tough lip encounter. I went full wild man which helped but without scotts tender loving words to guide my right foot all would have been for naught. Time to pop that Quad! And yes Scott exiting the wash to meet our nephew was a folly, but at least it was a good workout of a folly!
All aboard the struggle bus! all aboard!

I am past my Yokai Limit so this send was unbelievable. Somehow ripped a hole in my pointer with these comfy holds which makes no sense. Fun moves though. Could be 7 but soft 8 or solid 7 is fair.  Definitely a grade or two harder that Dyno Time low but not sure which climb that speaks more to.
Yessirreebobyankeedoodie! I have been reduced to a puddle of flesh. Maybe I need to do some of those new hip flesh runs. Cool Ball Ricks on this.
ascents.sectorName: Cabin Fever / The Perimeter / The Death Scream Area

ascents.comment: Cleaning up some fun easier lines now that I am a squashed banana. A glorious set of balls/knockers/knobs on this rig.  Sit start is a little meh
ascents.sectorName: Cabin Fever / The Perimeter / The Death Scream Area

ascents.comment: This must have been done by some bored lad or lass but I have yet found no information so I am dubbing it "An Ape Named Ape" until I hear otherwise. Start on Bubbatronic but from the jugs move right through a rad slot-gaston-thing making a big reach up and right to better holds. A little awk with the tiered landing/rock in the landing but that reach is a peach of a reach if you are hearin what I preach. I will put "FA" on 8a because as Jurassic Park taught us "Nobody Cares" but wouldn't dare to put "FA" on MP.

Obviously this is harder than the original... but only minutely so. 7B is what we call the "pyramid wrecker" so hard 7A Plu it is. Shoutout purple Totoro shirt getting all the compliments. Finally getting the recognition it deserves.
What a silly name. Honestly a better start than the original as it keeps the compression theme longer. The og start is just a cosmetic connection your mind mistakes for thematic. Again 7B oh so bad.
Thought it might be cool, then started thinking it was poop, then found an enjoyable sequence that was cool. We will call it cool poop. Fun working with a cumulatively exhausted Waffle.

Perfect name Kody! Getting the seconds ascent after Kody just makes it even more good. Great fun building that landing with the boys and making the slightly scary landing not scary at all. Great jugs lead to awesome feature with slightly techy top.  Ill drink to that!

Also quite wonderful. Already forgot all the names of the people I met today. Nice holds with fun moves, will clean up nicely. I think Jordan got the FA? If so ill change the name if I ever learn it has ha real one.

Worst of the bunch. Start as for the center line but move lefter through the easier more chossy holds. Not bad but not great. So funny that wince i started building my wall my outside climbing time has plummitted lol

No idea what the actual name is. Ill maybe fix it one day. This climb is the cool campus to the right of "When Life Gives You Lemons". Was originally told V8 but this thing is soft and glorious. Such a fun move. Gymtastic. I did not flash. boo. Good job shirley, first v8 flash for you? =P.
Absolutely wonderful. Thanks Daniel for the awesome bachelor party weekend. This was the perfect climb to start the day.

10 beers is too few for a handful of boys. Next time more beer. Another fake name because I just have no idea. On the direct opposite corner of "When Life Gives You Lemons". Started pretty high on a good right hand seam crimp and something opposing for the left. Got a high right foot and just slapped to a jug. Soft. Worked with with Nick. Thanks for organizing Nick!

Another one that I'm just slapping a fake name on. This is on the back side of "When Life Gives you Lemons", its that almost cool looking compression shelf thing. But don't let it fool you, its not that fun. Definitely knee bar crux, that right toe is tiny. Thanks Bryce for bringing a knee pad. Speaking of Bryce I hope your foot wasn't too fucked.  I started with the left hand on the awkward meat hook instead of the slightly lower crimp. Absolutely incredible that I managed to pull this, I guess I really just wanted to look good for Gabe! ;)

There are likely many variations on this wall but there is a ton of moss. I cleaned up enough to make the line go but I bet there are many many hidden holds still. This is the most obvious line on the slab which goes up the center with a big move to an obvious big edge.

Might be V4, has a pretty tough stand up top out move. On the obvious boulder start on the part of the rock closest to the road just below the right side of the long shelf of "Mineral King Rd."  There are some very cool edges on this rig. Luckily they run out before the crux standup. Calling this "Fire Force" as a shout out to anime, but also to the real life fire fighters (not animated) who helped protek the MK valley. Bc of their protection most of the brush surrounding this boudler was cleaned off which made it way more pleasant. As obvious as thsi boulder is I had not done it until today becuase of the annoying brush.

An obvious line I first visualized more than a decade ago. Follow the obvious right to left shelf feature by sit starting just below the right side of the shelf (same start as "Fire Force"). As all good lines go this thing is contrived and all holds above the quintessential shelf are off. Probably means there are a lot of variations but its rad.

Another one I envisioned more than a decade ago. on the left side of the boulder start relatively high on a left hand gaston and the namesake tooth hold for your right hand. That fucker has three bullet teeth which really dig in for a sweet and sticky grip. Do one move mini dyno to the lip. Cheyaah! This one DEFINITELY has lower start potential. Could be hard and good.

This is the most obvious boulder in all of MK because it is seen by anyone who has ever hiked at the Eagle-Mosquito trailhead. I would bet some of these lines have already been done but no worries. Start sitting a little akwardly near a rock in the landing to the right of the obvious ledge feature of (Mineral King Rd.). Its a pretty juggy hold. Move basically straight up through obvious good hold making a kind of tricky top out move which might use a mono.

Dubbing this boulder "Stormlight". This whole boulder is absolutely stellar. Seriously, its ludicrously good. It has probably a dozen total lines. You know this boudler is good becuase its like 3.5+ miles away and off trail but it had an anchor set up on the slab side! Damn this shit is dope. Anyway, this line is located on the steepest side of the boulder on the right side. Start sitting with a downpull crimp for your left and a right facing crimp for your right. Make an amazing big move to a crimp jug and bounce through some nice edges for a techy mantle.

Would be 5 starts but that right start hold is a little friable. sad. Left side of the steepets side of the boulder. Start compressing on arete and opposing crimp. Some interesting slaps gets you to another not gimme mantle. The perfect crimp above the lip makes it mucho enjoyablo. I cant believe how long I had to wait to finally see this boudler in person. Buddy system everyone. never forget. Worth the wait though.
Start as for Not a Woman but traverse left into "My Sun, My Moon, My Starlit Sky". Not that good really.

After getting up the infamous granite face once you start to enter the juniper trees on the final rise to the lake. Jag across eagle creek and find this rock. Start sitting on great holds low, throgh a high arcing dice into the air and land your heel right into that cup. Sploosh! Use the good heel to power straight up through a rad edge. Waaay harder than I expected. Looks maybe V2 but it put me on my ass a lot. Means is probably not V5 but it sure felt like it today.

Second ascent!!! Hell yeah Rod! This is Rods FIRST out door climb, hell, I think it was is FIRST EVER rock climb and it was an FA out in the middle of nowhere! This has to be some sort of record. Fun to hike with someone who can actually out hike me. SO proud of you for snagging this FA and stoked to see you become a bouldering nut. Also good name my dude.

Holy cow this may take the cake for best V0 in MK. Again on the left side of Eagle Creek after the granite face part of the trail. Somehow I had never looked at this boudler before but it has some of the coolest crisscrossing large quartz (or marble, what do i know im not a doctor) veins. It also has some juggy crack systems to make for a juggy good time. This is the most obvious line on the boulder starting in the center.  at the base of the crack on good holds.
Left side of the same amazing rock.
The same great rock starting on some xenos on the right.

Cannot give 5 stars because the flakes are hollow but it is dtop dead stunning.  One of the best backdrops for a boudler anywhere. and clocking in at about 18 feet this face has  a lot of climbing. ON the uphill side of the boudler start on two small crimps and make a tough-ishmove into a gaston, which puts you in to the massive flake system. Climb up via the flak to another massive edge and continue up. Try not to spam your reach and actually do a rock climbing move at the end, but since I was sans spotter on the flash FA burn I max reached to the lip. Cannot wait to get back to this boulder with the boys, both sad and non-sad alike.
Awesome xeno ladder on the Eagles crest side of the lake. Somebody must have done this already. Joey did it too! Woohoo! So fun doing this hike with Joey and Danbee!

On the Phlebotomist boulder, to the left of the tree is a short face with some cool xenos. Sit start with two of em, slap in some toe hooks out leftand derp up left hand to a gaston. Your ass swings out for a mildly entertaining thrutch.  not as easy as i expected

Start on the back right of the Knight Boulder and do some cool moves in some angled crimps until you can hit the top right arete and do a surprisingly hard rock over. I think a link up of this into Horseback Ride or vica versa could be pretty fun.

This surprised me! It's very cool and surprisingly easy compression. On the Knight boulder this is on the slot between the horse head and the adjacent boulder (back of the horse head).  Start sitting pretty low and slap up to a at cool rock over. Epona is one of my favorite fantasy horses ever so you know this climb is at least decent.

Pretty sure I tried this from the water years and years ago when the lake was full and was to scarred while wet. turns out its quite easy and quite nice, like a leisurely horseback ride. Landing is not great but climb is nice. Back left side of the Knight Boulder

I've looked at this potential line for a long time. Start as for MSMMMSS but make a huge move up and right to a Gaston. From their continue up and right through the depression in the wall. I ripped out part of the big Jug on the send go, but its still a jug so no difficulty change.
Extend the original line (My Sun, My Moon, My Starlit Sky) by starting way down and left where Less Fuzzy starts. Actually adds some cool moves and some enduro to this rad V2

On the snout side of the horse head feature, do a cool high pop up foot to get over the bulge. You can use holds on the left corner but make sure to stay on the actual horse face for full value. Landing is pretty bad with rocks and water so probably try not to fall

Requires late season when the lake is mostly dry because this boulder is mostly underwater. Once its dry enough there is an awesome flat landing for this incredible looking feature. It literally looks like a horse head or a knight chess piece. Start in the center of the face and go up and left through the honker xeno. A little tall but its so good. Tried years ago in hiking shoes and no pads, but with actual shoes its casual and fun!
Same difficulty as the better line. Start in the same spot but instead of going to the glorious xeno, go right over the horse head.

When there is water in the lake there is a pretty obvious big rock that essentially makes an Island. Not to be confused with the actual island further in the lake. There is a channel between the main split boulder and the flat topped boulder it leans on. If you start in the center of the channel and climb the flat topped boulder, you will have climbed this. When the lake is full this is completely underwater so must be done later in the season.
Of the underwaters, this is definitely the best. Big ol' holds, non wet landing and easy.

Start on the right side of the boulder and traverse left (through the start of 'Underwater') until you go far enough. Then top out  guess. Meh. I think there was a kinda hard move at the start but its been like 6 months so maybe v2? maybe easier? Who knows, this will probably never be done again so who really cares. ME thats who.

On the same higher tier as "Sex, Shower, and Hiking" at Mosquito 5 toward Eagle is this wall which has a cool reverse "N" system of cracks. Cyrillic has a backwards N in its alphabet hence the name. This line is the diagonal up and right line. Quite nice jugs, some smeary feet at the bottom but a good line. Might be V0.
On the Cyrillic N this is going straight up the left vertical crack. Might also be V0 cannot remember, its been too long. Good holds make it enjoyable.

Toward the north west side of Lake 2 there were a few small boulders. I hopped on this one that was a small boulder with a small freestanding roof. There were two crimps beneath the roof with yields a cool move to the lip and a decent lip encounter.

Shoutout to Beyrlsofcash with this name. Probably the coolest line on the Cyrillic boulder, sit start the right side of the reverse N system. Some nice lie backing leads to a few crux options. Nice and fun, good job Beyrlsofchache for figuring out the beta even with a tired body. Meow!

Dyno from a large hold to another large hold. Also at the same north west side of Mosquito 2 near a large felled dead Western Juniper. Did it with one shoe and a sock bc my other shoe was needed to film

Obvious splitter crack by where we camped at Mosquito 5. Its on one of the slightly higher tiers toward eagle lake. Starts hands, to fists then slightly off width for the finish although I lie backed the end. Named for a silly answer to "when should I be naked?". lol. Because this is a crack i feel like its likely someone else has done it but oh well.

On the same higher tier toward eagle is an amazing warm up wall with tons of variations and good holds / cracks throughout! I did 6 distinct vertical lines up this wall which is about 30 feet wide and ~11 feet tall on the left and ~ 8 feet tall on the right. Im going to just name these all 1-6 so bear with me. This one is pretty far left starting on a left facing edge/flake feature and going straight up.
To the right of the aforementioned left facing edge/flake, and to the left of the most obvious vertical crack. Start on a crimpy dish at about chest height and go up
Best of the lines on this wall. Go up the most obvious of the vertical cracks. Sit start
Sit start on a crack basically in the center of the wall. Right facing crack and some balance leads you to the top.
Stand start on a crack at about the right third of the boulder. Climb
Stand start another crack pretty far right on the boulder (but before the crack with plants in it)

Could be V2 but its pretty exploratory. So many cool features making for a fantastic warmup. This wall is just less the vertical so really lets you warm up those fingers and feet. If you do it twice in a row I guarantee you will use different holds.

Honestly this traverse is pretty rad. Cooler than the left to right because it finishes on the taller part of the boulder. Again awesome features on this pretty long 30ft traverse. Cool this way too bc the is crux is at the end.

A decent slightly delicate face compression thing to the left of Pangolin. Start to the left of pangolin standing on opposing holds. The first move smearing to get the foot up is probably the crux, but  its a bit delicate after that so good foot placement/trust is needed. Stay to the left of the arching Pangolin sloper feature finishing just to the right of the downclimb. Not great but it is one more okay climb in this relatively dense woodson area!
Wonderful crimps on this little guy. WIll certaintly add thsi to my South Slope warm up circuit. It faces north too which is great for avoiding some son!
Meh. Pull off the ground felt very hard then that was it. The right hand holds are pretty cool but its short and feet are meh and rock quality on left is meh.

It was decently hot today but starting on BOTH crimps under the roof seemed impossible. I started sitting with right hand on the obvious crimp and left hand opposing on the lip. First move was a hard hand heel match then the fun part starts! Surprisingly fun little compression guy with an odd top! Poor berylsofcash getting heat exhaustion: LR hits hard with the heat + sun sometimes. Definitely one of the toughest hikes out ever carrying as much as i can and rationing water! Newtopia cider afterward to celebrate being alive! My shoulders hurt.

No idea how I pulled this today, an it felt easy to boot! I think its one of those climbs where it gets disproportionately harder the more times you try. That hold will always be too sharp, but that's what makes it so rad. Locking off was too hard so just a big ol DP to that glorious dike pinch. A true lock off would b coo too. Sorry berylsofcash for trying to kill you in the heat today =P. 85 is monstrous at LR

Holy crowley that was close. Was tryna send fast to support berylsofcash on Shortness of Breath and I got myself mega flash pumped trying hard beta mid climb. I thought I saw the line but I was up there like... dang this doesn't work! lolz. Had to audible and only my incredible thigh squeeze power got me to the top. I cant even remember what I did but I did it, I remember that.
Def not V8 but some cool moves, to some jug choss, to a nice top out.

Incredible hard to discern where this thing was intended to go. Seem smost natural to trend right toward the top? Ill take it. Difficulty is pretty dubious too, harder than it looks. Heel toe cam is pcool.

Weekend in Mammoth with the Bae berylsofcash! Its the Margarita Festival, we pulled!! Anyway, my 2015 Ford Focus could not make it to Hartley... popped tire on an attempt. Had to put the spare on, somehow turn around and navigate back down. Spare is flat now too. Lets climb! Hike ain't too bad from the Freeway. We got as lucky as ducks get by running into those rad dudes of whom I have forgotten all their names. They not only drove Me and Mary Ann and our pads down but gave be a beer and pumpe dup my spare! I owe you big. Oh this climb is nice.
yes, its fun.
Fun, this is.
Drink all the beers. This thing has cool features.
It's NOT easy for people like us (wet people that is).
Fun bouldering so close to your house!!! How rad Mr Girth and Mrs Waffle! Left or right?! I don't even remember but I know it was important
He and She did the stand as warm up. (I did not)
Start as for "Nightcrawler" but immediately exit right  after the first right hand bump, directly over your starting heel

My beta feels broken, hence the V7. Mr Girth on the other hand is just a dick. I had no chance of doing it the way everyone else does. These sweaty sausages on that angled crimp! in the direct sun! no way hose!! Props to the human waffle for throwing herself a this thing like a thing that gets thrown. I just hit a small directional crimp then spanned all the way to the good hold
Pfun. Plittle, pshort but pfun. Chilling with my beryls of cash!
Start as per Finish Your Dinner but don't go right at all.  Hit the lip match and mantle. Tough with the tree at your back. Well Tough or dumb, one of the two.
Where did Kody fall on this!?
Static version better than OG.
Looks like is should be cake but then it ain't. Tricky slippery top.

Don't know if this is the correct name. I think maybe it's the stand to Spicy Beaver? Anyway far right line on Darkside Boulder. Decent little guy. I need the V Points to break my 75 point record from 8 years ago. All i gotta do is snag the Choadler and im good to go.... he said.

I did this wonky, whats new? Speaking of being surrounded by fish, this is my second time to Pine Mountain and last time I came with the lovely Andrew and the lovely Drea. That was literally like 8 years ago!!! (10-03-2016). Those same fish swam with me today! How cool right!?
Hard to grade but yes that press is pretty pure. Gunning for that V point record from last time! Last time I was here was October 3rd, 2016 and I whipped up 75 V Points.
The Choadler is harder. Change my mind.
Those features got me wet. Well actually I'm always wet because apparently I am a greasing god. What an honor.
That was some ludicrous beta I used. Seriously one of the oddest sequences ive ever done. There was a press cross, an intentional knee push. Odditys for sure, but entertaining
Short but enjoyable, sit looks like it could be cool. Meeting the frolf boys at Pono! Classic. Chase should have come for that open mike!
Rad slopers, but that first move seemed real not fun. That akward landing rock makes pulling on meh. After teh first move tho it was my bread butter and toaster.
Cool to finally check out castle! This climb was nice.
Tried to use static beta, I should have known jumping to jugs was the way! Great line.
This this was nice.
Cool Jergs but movement felt a little odd. Did stand and sit. sit is better.

Nothing like a good ol' one-of-anything to change a weekend in bishop with my honey to a friendsgiving in the bay with the sandbox. Good thing he flashed that thing years ago  at the Cliffs of Id; A lot of frolf would not have been had otherwise. A great use of a one of anything. Dela, Beer, GGP, Winery Frolf, Friends, Beer Die, Homer, good thigs. Thanks nate! Also shoutout Banka for being rad.
Def a unique and fun line. Nice to get on after the crowds went home
Zat vas Paumpy! Very nice climb with satisfying top moves. Did stand and sit. Our boys b frolfing today.
Almost did not flash! Kind of a hard single move, but its a good one! Don't really like climbing with other people anymore lawlz
I found many hard ways to to the throw to the lip. I rock. Very cool long line with awesome knockers at the beginning. Good thing I b good at  mantling.

I don't think I am allowed to take flash for this, I did Mr Witty a decade ago, but I did do it first burn today and i was very proud of myself so i am taking it. My cold tips actually didn't feel wet. Thank god I did it in one go otherwise it would have never happened. THanks scott for remembering mono. Now i can finally project Less Poetry Please!
Good mantle and fun low move. Maybe I should restart my lost ambition to check everything V7 and under in the tablelands?
Nice jergs. Way to go honey on Serengetti!!

This is a big shoutout to Scott. Without me he would never have tried this thing, but likewise, without him I would have never sent. We complete each other. I doubt this was still an undone project but as of the new guidebook it was still listed as a project "Erik's Arete" in sleepy hollow. Crazy triple bump big span radness. Also small shoutout to our own Erik with a K, and also fishbowl. If Scott truly got the FA I got the second, but who cares anyway, its only a model.

Gobble Gobble is three stars! True that fish bowl. Recommending this because the rock is bullet and the moves are fun. Also because I had such a good time in this wannabe ice caves with Scott, Mary Ann and Erik (not with a c). You guys all rock. In the book this has a comma.

Oooohh Whee hes's crimping! Crimping real hard! Great to see E-Rock and climb silly obscure things with him and Scott. Loving my uncanny ability to get people to try things lol! Speaking of obscure, this climb is amazing. I think I cheated and started a little too high, but this climb is cool as nails and hard as nails. Highly recommend for you slab folks.
This is way better than zero stars! Especially since the turtle head protruding feature is so cool the wall begs to be climbed. Was fun mantling in that dihedral in my cruisers.
I think I may have actually don't Pirates Booty V4 and called it Tim's Obscurity V7. Hard to tell with the terrible descriptions but the new guide moved the number so we will just fix it in post.
I love getting Woo to do things.

Not gonna lie Crabs on My Nipples took a lot out of me. Darn Crustaceans! Good session here with Erik-undercling-ripper-mcgee, Rick, Woo and Banka. Movement wise quite nice. That starting hold is rad.... but friable. That last go took all my mustard so I'm glad it went.

Since most of us don't climb V13, or even V11.. wait a second am I now in the minority? Do most people climb V11 now? Damn I'm weak. Anyway I started this 8 foot boulder 7 feet up and took 8 full points for it. Funner than expected, Choss knew I love silly climbing like this. Started spanned with pad stack between left hand sloper and the black knob.
Not as good as Raggedy Ann but very fun and the landing is flat. These climbs should have chalk more often! Fight that barn door boys and girls!

Believe it or not this was favorite climb from the trip. Its such a good lip traverse that I'm really sad its not closer to the main area or at least another well known boulder. This send kind of sums up the trip: obscure boulders that are rad, amazing friends, complete exhaustion, beer. Good times. Thank you Drew for making this trip possible and thank you everyone who was present!

How is this thing not more done!? So good. The trav is a little silly but the meat of this climb is perfect. A big move from cool crimps to a bonafide JERG. Landing is a little bad but with a few pads its very safe. I love this type of beautiful DP.

This felt like a miracle. Scott and I started right hand good right facing sidepull and left hand a crappier opposing left hand sidepull out left which is NOT how Andy Liu did it. Its harder this way and I think better. You get an awesome drop knee. So proud of Woo for breaking his rest day to try this with us. Very painful. Got em!!!
Book has this at V1 and its pretty nice so I say thats fine. Whatevs. Ill be back for shite arete!
Cool start holds fun mantle! I wanted to deo everything on this boulder but no star climbs at JTree can be so hard!
enjoyable. Rich enjoyed this one too. Speaking or Rich and fat, we did the Great Chasm which was pretty fun! The "coffin" isn't that hard and would recommend as a quick climbing detour

Another one that the sister rocked. A little spicy up high but I knew once she was up there she would nail it! This little close area has some good easy stuff! Speaking of Hot and Juicy, I almost got the ultra classic Streetcar Lie Down start! Next time for sure.

Amazing visit from the sister and her Alaska family! We got her on waves and up rocks!! Send train with me rich and Karen! A little tall for years off the couch but my sister rocked it!. Can you believe this was my parents FIRST time to Joshua Tree. I cannot. Pops said his favorite part was climbing! We got the legend Jack Vasko to scramble. It was loot my dudes. The nephews were a blast too, glad I brought that Maya Flya! Pokemon Go forever.
Tried first go in cruisers. No go. This be good tho. In the book this is 5a and it has a hyphen not a space "Semi-Precious"

Start chest height on a bunch of choss to the right of Mr Long arm in that crevice. Move left through the cool ledge and wrap all the way around the detaching block instead of going up. Not terrible but definitely not good.

Probably not a FA either but I am a troll here so

Same start as Mr. Longarm for off rout the entire rail. Go left instead with a decent shoulder move in the the detaching block. Wrap around left and finish that way. Not as good as the OG but def worth doing if at this boulder.

Unlikely an FA, but will still log on 8a as such.

If someone gets mega inspired and actually digs out the landing this might actually be pretty cool, but currently its one of those lie down starts where you are so close to the ground that you cannot actually tell if you are climbing or not. Start beneath the OG holds literally less than a foot off the ground. Move into the OG start holds then do the normal climb. 

Probably not an FA either.

Probs V8, but that means poison control is probs v7. Oh wells. Shark tooth is still hard. 

That dank dust is dank!! Oh yeah good job marina on that thing over there.

Oh yeah also happy bday to the one and only chaseypoo. Glad to play more frolf this weekend than bouldering lolol. Good times
Middle finger was the better choice.

Is my home wall helping me crimp!! I do love those escape dot crimps. 

I remember years ago chase telling me how easy this was so i was too embarressed to even try. Knowing food was inevitable =P. Today i somehow flashed. wowzers
I can actually climb? What a miracle. Good times on obscure goodies with chase scott and the crew.
Rad warmup. Good height.
Cool. Feet are worse than they look. Other Scott bringing some weird juju. That gummy work toss was hilarious.
Blew the flash bc i didn't realize there was a stand start and I dropped off from the top jug lolol. Some of those holds feel bad, and only get worse with more and more sun + sweat
If you got the span, the stand start is the crux. Cool extension on an already cool climb. Michelle stoked that you and Luna made it out for some great camaraderie.
That was not nice and easy. Start is rad top is meh. Was hoping this would be cool so I could recommend it to others but alas I could not do that. Shoutout glove climbing and the Little Arete V4
Def a softie but its very fun. Good second go train with Mr. Girth. Both of us missing the big first move on the flash.

I actually have some really normal dreams. Well maybe because they are so normal they are abnormal. I mean I dream about doing yardwork: pulling weeds, mowing the lawn, trimming the trees, digging holes; that sort of stuff. Best part is usually when I wake up I get to do it again, but better this time since I've already done it once. This climb was fun, good working with the davids, and chase. Happy birthday chase.
Backlog. We need more of these in areas with tons of too hard stuff. So much fun, Standing one of anythign bet to do with with them mittens.

Based on Scotts star algorithm this would be 5/5 stars. (1) Height/landing, (2) Aesthetic, (3) Movement, (4) rock quality. (5) Pureness. Well i guess MP says there is a V8 right exit so maybe 4.5 stars, losing half a star on pureness. But like Toad I award it the happening half start since I could do it and Scott couldn't. boo yah! Home wall doing me good on the crimpers!
Not fully warm yet and this felt nails, i say NAILS! Get me a hammer bc this was NAILS. honestly probs a softy, but still a goody. Many sweet grips.

Definitely a must do of the area. I'm falling back on Scotts star mechanism but is very pragmatic which is nice: (1) Height/landing - landing is a little awk, but its safe. Still earns star.  (2) meh aesthetic, so it does not earn this star (3) movement (4) rock quality (5) pureness. So I guess 4 stars (like I logged). Different beta than Scott but yeah, I'm a different human: believe it or not. Almost snagged the sit but I'm a tired boy. Def not V9.

Holy fuck Triassic is way better than advertised. Maybe that's intentional? Anyway I did nor realize I was saying 
"Cretaceous" incorrectly for God knows how long. Actually God doesn't know, why would he pay attention to that? Also doe he even exist? Anyway, south-ish from Cretaceous there is a corridor with a face that has two rad opposing slopers with bit rail at the bottom. I did that. I did that to add to the confusion. Your Welcome. Start right hand flexy hold left hand pressing on said rail.

The top of this thing is scary! You got pinball potential and the top jug is a chicken head! Anyway, if you are reading this you probably read my stand start FA. For 2 extra points start on the rail with a high heel and pull up to the flexy hold. Awesome feature, if landing was better this for sure would have been done by OG trolls.

First flash on this bad boy! I'm a proud boy. Also I really though Scott was spotting me for the mantle. Turns out he wasn't. he just poked his head over from Thump to watch. I heard his voice and was instantly reassured. I must say, my trust in you is big time because I fucking did the mantle.

Top is a sandbox. Toe hook beta is fun but not necessary. The half rotation campus in was easier. But this climb is about being memorable and hell yeah it was memorable. Pinch epicing was also memorable. Nice.
A perfect warm up. Remember pull out not down. Don't be a duchebag. Oh i did this barefoot for no apparent reason but it was nice

Scott makin MOVES on Trents mom. PLURAL. That climb is way funnier when you know a Trent. Anyway, the grips on this are all time! Movement too! A tad contrived but it is fun as fuck and aesthetic as fuck. First climb in my live using both a ladder and a rope and let me tell you... it helps immensely! Seriously saves SO much energy. So awesome. Good climb.
Multiple years in the making. So much fun this boy. No single move is harder than V5 but damn that's a lot of moves for a boulderer. Good times with Ned and nick.

Awesome climb with sweet grips as the MP says. Good ol' steep roof with jugs leading to sweet as compressive crux! Felt something pop in my knee on the flash, had my right heel in that big hueco for the first hard right hand slap before the lip. It wasn't loud though so I think that means nothing tore. Definitely wont right heel for a while but luckily the one I really want this trip "The Beautiful Boobies" AKA "Playmate of the Year" can be doen without a right heel. May have been too cold at 9 am by the river to warm up here. Oh well, full sweep on this with the boyz

Tired boyz. Failed on Playmate of the year again. 3rd day on but feels more like 4th day bc day 0 was like 10 hours of shoveling snow and post holing. Got to the blind throw on the flash go and thought maybe this was soft, then proceeded to not be able to do multiple moves for a long while. Finally pieced together the puzzle with Ned and Nick and took her to the top. Fattys for dinner was  nice! GPT4 gonna take our jobs!

Movement masterpiece. Sit start feels a little forced, but it does set up that amazing Gaston sequence. So many good moves. I love that this climb feels like its slowly decreases difficulty over the course of the climb which is super rad bc you are getting more tired but its getting easier. I wonder how much work the FAers did to excavate this rig. Cicadas do burrow underground so maybe the name is a reference to that. First move of White Buffalo is so frustrating.

Too cold. I did not enjoy being this cold. If only that left hand crimp was a better hold this would be an All Star ~V4. As is its a good V3 with one hard move. Still cool. I realized that whole under cling feature is glued / cemented which makes sense I guess, but still loses some purity. The Flu area is pretty coo! Shout Ned for his impeccable form on the top of this!
I am so tired. Wrecked really. Cleaning boulders really should not count as a rest day. Good end to the day to really put a fork in my ass. Fun climbing.

Three dimensional climbing at its finest. Seriously so rad. Those starting tufas are in-creh-dah-blay! Pretty sure I would have flashed if it was not 22 degrees out. Impossible to warm up and impossible to stay warm for more than like 2 moves. The rock is a really big ice cube. On the flash I stopped feeling my hands on the third move and kept climbing but eventually I grabbed a hold wrong but could not tell. Shoutout Pinch for validating his trip with this one, and shoutout Ned for finishing the epic with a send!

This boulder may now be my favorite right fork warm up area. This and midget give a great variety of holds and movement to get warm. The next generation link up of Dustbuster into Midget and back into Dustbuster while eliminating all the big holds is the perfect end to a warm up.
This has a standalone boobie which is nice.

I think I've tried this thing every trip to goes. Multiple sessions last year and the year before that. So stoked to finally put it down, and pretty darn cleanly I must say. So may bodily pains in my body, and many butterflies in my basked but pulled boys. Extruded even. I feel like a million Buckaroonies!!
ascents.sectorName: Cabin Fever / The Perimeter / The Death Scream Area

ascents.comment: Flashed so obviously cannot be V9. Very cool moves. That Chat crew was pretty entertaining. I wonder what sort of weird things they said about us afterward lol. I can be quite a raging eccentric.
Props to Ned on completing a rad 7-7-7!! Nice work. This climb is pretty rad! Unique and fun. Nice hanging with Hal!!
I feel like 2 million Buckaroonies!!!
ascents.sectorName: Cabin Fever / The Perimeter / The Death Scream Area

ascents.comment: Damn that shit was dope. Feels so unlike Joes, but in a wonderful kind of way. Great slabbing this one with ultra satisfying finish.

Close last year, felt good to clean her up. Everyone should get on the sweet right exit "An Ape name Ape". It was way too cold again. 22 degrees when we got back to the cars... and the wind was wipping... its too much. Good quick evening session with Ned after his super fun meetings. The quick sesh meant we got to snag a nice Fattys with our boy Scotticus
A little friable and a sandbox at the top but a pretty good warm up with juggos.
Honestly a decently cool move from the good incut slot to the lip... but either I started wrong or this is V3. I will likely do again if warming up at Pimpin Jeans so thats a plus.
Huh. I guess this is a climb.

Handful of gos. Had to try pretty hard on this boy. Thought I might finally be strong enough to cruise, but no, we are not at cruising altitude my dudes and dames, we are not. Fun climb and with good company to boot! Also shoutout Ned for making his argument for one of the best last days in joes by pulling Gurkha AND Point Break. Fantastic last day of a fantastic trip! Drive safe!

Ave Maria

Almost guaranteed not to be an FA but ill take those coveted 8a points until someone corrects me. An easier sequence could drop the grade to V8 probs but whatever. Start as For Cretaceous Sit, but after the first move hitting the big undercling move left utilizing another small undercling to lunge out left to a cool pinch block on the left arete. Paste a foot on and jump to the perpetually dirty crack jug and swing away dear boys.

My goal this year is 10 V10s and my first V11 (time to mega proj fight club).  With this tick I have my first soft V10 of 2023, woot woot! Second session. Was gonna give up but the weather took a turn for the worse so Scott gave up on climbing for the day (he yoyo-ed alot today) and suggested we take a nice walk to look at boulders. We found the Bad but couldn't find anything in golden ladle. Anyway with a physical and mental break I came back primed and proper. With a subtle foot beta change early I took this down using one of the most aggressive and loud slaps I have made to date. Cant wait to use that sound bye in a remix at some point. Thanks scott for filming until the end. Gold. Soft.

This deserves the upgrade. Granted Scott and I are tired and its too cold outside to actually properly fuel your muscles but dang that was a lot. Had to try so so hard. Why is it snowing again? At least the little ponds are freezing over to make beautiful, thin and clear ice porcelain sheets! I cant believe how happy those ices made me.

I know you aren't supposed to log stands that were not established by the FA-ers but I had trouble reading the Eon Red description and this looked fun and easier that Eon Blue. Cool Knee bar makes it worth adding an easier start I think. Fourth day on, so squeezing in a tiny bit more climbing and now looking forward to 2 rest days =D.
This deserves the hype. Very nice. Crux reach feels decently hard for V1 but wonderful holds and movement leave a delectable taste in the mouth hole. Finally some sunny nice weather!

This should probably not be V0. Find a V0 climber who can do this and ill show you a unicorn. This is the awesome multi ledge feature on the backside of "Golden" which features a mid  climb mantle! Pretty freaking rad. Scott epic-ing on the "stand up" post mantle part. lololol. Very fun and not scary despite MPs PG13 distinction

This might honestly be the most impressive thing I have sent this trip. I like that dudes comment "Square Peg, Round Hole" because it is just so damn poetic. A climb whose grade is super finger girth dependent. On the go I miraculously pulled off the ground I sent. Subtle left toe in a seemingly unused space was crucial for me. The crux was definitely squeezing as much sausage as possible into a small space.

Is this name a shoutout to crushing soft things? Like crushing cute little baby bunnies? Because damn this thing might honestly be V5... for anyone who thinks otherwise go do Wrecking Ball first. Was stoked to piss my pants a little on this but, naw dawg naw, no piss, I just casually micro hopped to the lip, keeping my left hand on and 0 swing... I wonder if the start holds have gotten better over the years? Maybe they used to be bad? I could see that bumping the difficulty a bit? Anyway, V5 + 2 scare factor = V7. Obviously this is a dyno so it will be significantly harder for shorter folks, give it the grade it deserves. Also sorry for being a dick.

AKA the perfect warmup. As contrived as imaginatively possible. And scott and I are imaginative folks; im talking about vision; VISION! Start as for Dustbuster, but off route the two good hole like holds. After the first move left hand span right all the way to the boob on midget. Once established on the midgets boob,  bup right hand to the crip and go back left into dustbuster with a MANDATORY cross from a left had crimp to the sweet as hight crimp of Dustbuster. When topping out be careful not to use the off routed holds. Probably not an FA but I like to reward my imagination.
Meh. Couldn't quite do last year so good to tick off. Got some fun moves. I wish the start holds were a little more obvious: both the book and MP don't really do a good job.

God I love working remote. This thing is nice-ish. Not as good as the incredibly contrived warm up line Scotty and I threw together, but its k. Was expecting this to be harder since its so short. Our warm up line is harder so that is def getting V7. Also I did not realize I could use the holds from "Midget" so I made this harder than it needed to be.
Up an down a few times to find / clean holds and warm up. Very nice, yes its very nice. Scott is a hero btw, had my biggest ever witness high seeing you send Lonseome. Great job you man amongst men.
Some sweet grips. Nice of the lord almighty to give a decent warm up area at the damn boulders

Consensus says hard for the grade and I agree. I even found alternate feet first beta to avoid that crux second move and I still think it felt hard for 7. Trip fatigue may be setting in, playtime is not over.

Honestly this may have been my favorite on the nerf wall. A few of those pockets allow a sweet as thumb catch which just feel orgasmic. Good holds make a climb so enjoyable.  Barely enough non snowy space up top to top out.

Okay this thing is hard. Like its honestly harder than the flu.. no way V5, original guide says "good" right hand side pull, that thing is trash. I wanted to double upgrade but I will start the bidding at hard V6. My beta was freaking rad with techy heel on the left facing crimp, hit the gaston below the lip, then rose! Rampage day with Scott! Wish I sent more so I could prove to 8a how much we hit today... Flu, Cabin Fever, 7 Mile, Cyndicate and Playtime is Over. That's both forks and new joes! What a day!

Never have I seen a climb with a more diverse consensus. I see 6, 7, 8 and 9. Wow. Def not V9, probably not V6. I could see V7 or soft 8. I'm gonna reward myself with some cheese here and take the 8. Taller than you expect and top was dusty and snowy. Really should have scoped it but oh well, I had to put my wizards hat on and quest. Cool moves and holds; really quite surprised this doesn't get done more. Def easier than 5% tint... riddle me that. Thanks Scott for being a strong dependable man. I know you got me.

Really should have flashed, but I got the flash butterflies and flopped. Using wills as the master standard, this is not easier than wills, and thus cannot be V7. QED. Its also not easier that 5% tint but that's a whole different story. Very fun moves and for how close this is to Big Joe area (its at the 7 mile marker) it ought to see more attention. I'm giving it the recommend bc yeah, it was fun and it doesn't get done much. Also huge shoutout to Scott for having one of the best trips ever and finishing on a fucking high note. Congrats on Lonesome AND your freak send of Barely Legal. It was my honor to bear wittness and how fitting to finish our trip with playtime is over. Back to reality my dear and loyal readers.

Props to Kody for putting up more dope boulders at Tram and giving me the excuse to get back out this far. I got to scared to do this climb years ago by myself, but with DWoo supporting me I had what I needed. Great experience of a climb. Stoked to get back here for Shutts Squeeze and TotK.

Lip start to what I have been calling the "Bestiality Project".  Located about half way between Full circle and Control tower, the stand starts reaching high to some shit on the lip. The proj starts on the left hand wide pinch and right hand opposing side pull. Thought Drew might cruise this one, but instead he got violently ill and didn't even climb lol. Feel better my dude. Shoutout to an amazing bday weekend, specifically to AK and Slimb who flew down to make it basically a birthday week chocked full of activities. First Olympic W in a while. Also, Aden may have done this top out already.

What a refreshing trip to Portugal. I was DREADING this work trip after last year, but I am so glad it turned out to be amazing. Staying in Setubal vs Troia was a boon (I was 1 mile away from InWall!), and more flex in REPMUS schedule meant I actually got on real rock!!! I was sans pad, and combined a tourist day with climbing so I simply wanted that Days Climbed and Crags Climbed Metric. This line is a bit forced but it is the most climbed on 8a.nu. If I come out next year I'm definitely getting a proper day in Sintra!!
Nice jugs. Only problem is it is what makes Incha-La contrived.

This crag blew me away. I was at the "quinta da regaleira" earlier, then swung by incha-la (parked 3 miles away, so had a nice yog), and figured id check this crag out since hey, its on the beach and has sand which might be cool since I don't have a pad. It delivered. SUCH a beautiful spot. And the wall here is RAD. I mean the wall has: V8, V4, V7, Proj, V10, V12, V10, V9, Proj, V11, Proj, V7/8. Definitely got a bit sandy, and its a bit slippery but awesome holds and rock quality with great ambiance. IM glad there is at least one easy climb on this wall so I could log this journal entry.  There were surfers out and I wanted to surf so bad! Good thing Seb brought me the next weekend for some double overhead magic at Guincho. Also saw sunset here which was nice. Oh yeah this climb is p-good. Drop off but whatevs.

Wow. It wont let you add a "soft" flag if you are the one adding to to 8a. I don't really think this is V9, but it is harder that Pimpsqueek soo who knows except its definitely soft. This is the link up of Crimpsqueek into Pimpsqueek via a fun large rightward move from the large huecos to the big flat hold before the fridge feature. Nice to first go Pimpsqueek again after all these years, and yes it is still soft. This line took a few goes to figure out the big move but it was fun. The solo drive up to levy this time was incredible. Left Thursday after work and had a few wonderful stops on the way up to get in Saturday evening: Chelsea in SB, Ryan + Dustin + Daniel + Nick at Delavega, Scott in the middle of Oregon.

This feature is unreal. Like totally nuts. I've been to Mad Meadows many times and never seen this. Gimmicky for sure and dabby as all holy hell but I will still recommend because nature is amazing and so cool to see insane way rock can be formed.

Holy ballz what an adventure. I had no idea what I was signing up for when Drew said we were going to Kingslayer.... cheers to double padding with the boys, 8o minute  drives, carrying way too much weight (shoutout ladder / entertainment system holder), Love is Blind in the Throne Room, insane pain in my shoulders and hips, searching for holes in the dark, unbelievable flash by drew, many falls and laughs with surprisingly no injuries, shuffling pads through crawlspace approaches, too little food, maybe no lost items, stinky farts, 1:30am bed times, letting out our inner assholes, and more relevantly this amazing face with a perfect mantle. Took a bit to suss the beta, but I ate the mantle like I do.

I saw this and knew I wanted to do it. Squeeze mc Squeeze. My right leg didn't hurt which was nice. Classic hangry Drew, he did finally find us though and he was very happy about it. Good job Josh Jacobs for giving my boys something the cheer about during my send: it felt good. I cant tell, am I decently strong or is this really soft?
HOW is that v4 so hard. THis is significantly harder than Busted IMHO. Naturally I skipped the pinch bc that is an imaginary hold. Nico is a mad man.

Wowo. Only a handful of goes today. Honestly did not expect this on this trip since its a bit finger strength critical and that's always been my weakness. Maybe I am actually stronger than I expected! How nice =D. Wanted to take 10 bc not my style, but Chaaaaaarmed only took 9 and I don't want to be more of a bitch than him.

I misread the guidebook. I thought this rad dyno was "The Locksmith V8" but apparently this rad dyno doesn't even have a name. Direct mantle would be even more dope. I mantled before rounding the corner.

Edit (November 6, 2023) I found the name via Instagram. "Lock Down". Also 8a removed the "Area" option when adding a route so I cannot create this under Leavenworth/The Locksmith lol.
I love this feature and this feature loved me. Next year the low.

Harder than expected but very pretty rock, good movement and very aesthetic ambiance. Many tries, little rest, many fails. Can't believe no one else tried with me. Thought it was V5 based on Guidebook but V6 seems fair.
Awesome line. Wet Top. Nipples. Don't forget to Yeet.
The way I did this was really effing hard. Also so moist and slippery. Also body is beat. Good last day Nico and Drew miss ya already. Areas climbed metric baby!

I wanted to take the points but the sea of soft let me know I should to the right thing and downgrade. le sigh. Very fun though. On the pre send urn my left hand ripped on the big move and I had a wonderfuly swhirley whirley. Took more burns to do King Kong.

Am I not good at searching 8a? Are there virtually no logs of this climb? It's quite good. Hard. But good. Good thing we all have big biceps right Erik? Quality time hanging with the crew, talking anime doing some sack toss, and being boisterous. Crazy that there are actually left facing feet to make this lip traverse doable without heels. Achilles is in luck. Agree that this is probably harder than Johnney Appleseed for a big powerful boy like me.

Very good this boy. And very V8. Maybe even hard V8. But then again maybe not. One two to the lip for a wonderful time. Chaarmed. Speaking of "Chaarmed", Scott pulling the miracle send on Thunderdome Low. Good to see Erik too. Huzzah!

Couldn't quite pull the proj, but at least I pulled the days climbed metric. Short but actually fun. Ate shit into on the first move once which was entertaining. Thanks for all the psyche and support on Practitioner Scott! Next season for sure.

This should be upgraded. Always remember the best way to set a good 5 is to set a 4 and grade it 5. That dunk though. The sun behind the mountains I was talking about, but, that move to the lip is also sack. (36)

Scott helping me find the right feet for the underling move then I ate the mantle. nom nom. Scott didn't quite eat it first try, well technically he did off the boulder, but then he ate after eating. And really it wasn't not a bad eat, just a normal fall. Don't look up Bad Water Productions Darth Vader + Yoda.(32)

Dang if the landing wasn't so annoying this climb would be awesome! Starting sequence is a gem (naturally pronounced "gym" bc that's what I do), and the namesake lightening crack is d o p e. Final moves are tricky, would be nice to go down on it but instead you gonna use that two finger weird thing well, weirdly. Scott somehow mustering enough juice to generate off dat sloper which is good bc we didn't pad that part. (23)

YEEEEET BOOOOOYYYYSS!!!  Memory certainty has a recency bias but this is my favorite end to a trip I've ever had. Yes I'm taking 10 because I deserve it after going beyond plus ultra to pull this. Third day on and already a rampage of a day. Scott and I know hot to turn the try hard on and make the improbable possible. The double extra mantles on the top out are quite cool. Fans are a game changer for me: thanks for being my yeet boy Scott. Amazing trip in Leavenworth thanks again to all my dear friends: Scott, Akhil, Drew, Ned, Jasper, Nico, Erik, Amy (spelling?) and Tai (spelling?). One last shoutout to the incredible send off dinner. Chefs kiss. Next time lets get an air bnb in town. (58)

Trickier than I expected! A handful of goes, although in honesty I didn't want to send until my Scott arrived. He supplied psyche, a spot and a cruxy downclimb ladder placement. Great climb. Perfect start to my last day rampage at Mountain Home! (8)

A much harder run and jump than expected. I thought it was gonna be a bucket. I really enjoyed the top lock off move off that bad foot at the bottom of the namesake crescent feature. The boys are stoked to have service so they can service themselves with some TNF. (43)
Some cool features, but did not climb as good as I wanted. Mantle was harder than expected. (48)
If you can pull that first crimp move this is an absolute gimmie... very fun and more pure than Geronimo honestly. No splashing needed. First go after sending geronimo. Bang Bang! (16)

Feelings are both wonderful and terrible. Wow.... Acknowledging my emotion and feelings is what I've been working on this past year but damn some feelings are just so heavy.  Good things this climb is long, those 2 minutes were the most distracted and present I've been in a hot minute. Bottom moves were hard, mantle was cake, don't worry drew you'll get it next time. Also shoutout drew for a fun trundle from Power Animal to Poor and Famous.
ascents.cragName: Beehive Area / Secrets of the Beehive

ascents.comment: One of the best in the Sads and also one of the most sandbagged in the Sads. This is every ounce of V8. A miracle my left foot didn't blow. Couldn't quite get it up to the big hold so just toed down on some tiny edge. Today was a "good" day. Thank you Lisa, thank you Woo and thank you Drew.
Let the rocks heal my soul! Good to get out here with the boys. Glad traffic was only +3.5 hours! I pulled. Squeeze for me = softie.

That first move is otherworldly. Felt impossibly finicky until I decided to just squeeze really hard and smear even harder. Pleasure working this with 6 Inches of Luxury, A Poor Mans 3 Inches, Lynn and Preston.... those last two need better stripper names. Thanks Preston for instilling hope, sorry about those fingies. We also somehow lost Preston today soo that was neat.

(Tilt Shift Left Var.) I also did the weird left version. Start on the same holds but go left to friable holds then rejoin the main line at the jug.  May have taken me more burns than the OG but my right leg is still healing from Heartless in Joes in March so I couldn't heel as good. A good excuse to touch this amazing boulder some more.

This thing is the loot-ness. Much my style nom nom nom. I pulled before yer boys Woo, Scott and Rick which was good for my soul. Need that healing baby.  To be fair they were warming up when I was already rapid firing. This hike was further than I expected.
A beauty shared with some beautiful boys.
This thing is awesome. It made me happy to see how many people know Aura Bora!! Thanks Scott for the Viderbation material, heavens know I need it right now.
A boulder so great you get to do it twice! Seems to be a trend this trip. Fun variation. Cool to finish on such large boyos.

Wow. Many many burns over the years but somehow pulled first burn today. I guess I can latch things now? Thank goodness for the wonderful warm up at Jones'n Scott! Rad to nerd out to some anime with Richie!
Good warm up on some more friable jugs up high! Start moves are  actually pretty cool, will warm up on this again.
Meh. too chossy to trust in cruises but it can be incorporated into decent warm up circuit

Scott filmed all my good sends this trip. Praise be! Pure compression beta all the way, don't use any of those face crimp holds. So my style, I loved this thing. Fourth day on and still have this much Hutzpah?! THe depressive energy is so strong and deep my dudes and dames.  Infinite reservoir of strength. I think I might add Atlas to the potential V12 list...

I cannot shout out my Psyche Crew enough 100% would not have been possible without them. I had given up but was convinced for "one more go" like 8 times; each with a collaborative micro adjustments for holding the swing. That move felt impossible for me. The secret was pull up higher and throw that right foot around the corner. My left arm literally did nothing but somehow stayed on. Full horizontal swing on the send thanks Kevin for the stellar pics. The Telescoping ladder deserves a shout out all on its own. I cant wait for Ladder Sports in the 2024 Olympics. Scott with the current bottom run record at 19 seconds in Unsupported Balance. Our new friend with the highest rung count with 4 in the Unsupported Ascent Category. Some other shout outs: Drew for the 'best spotting award' and not getting bored, Kevin for photos and not freezing his balls of despite wearing only shorts, Lynn for Send Wheat Thins, enforcing my rests and preventing another lost watch, Scott for being a Pink Marshmallow, Woo for being able to support a full weight drew with his neck, Rick for leaving his torch in his pocket. You guys all rock, these positive memories helping dilute my pain. Slowly moving on

Real sweet this pony. Features are beauty. Top move is a little not as good but overall a great climb. A few burns, and nice warm up for mounting that White Whinocerwous awound the kworner. Scott is the god of psyche and support. Thanks my dude. You have singlehandedly filled my viderbation bank. Kinky.
I WODE DA WHITE WHINOCERWOUS!

Dubious start? I started with my left foot low on the good rail of "Little Pony" which was a pretty cool tension move if you are long enough. Grades are made up. Shoutout the people who finally commented on my Naruto jacket, that meant a lot.

Climb the slab to the left of "Turd in the Reflecting Pool" but don't use your hands. You can use your face/chin if need be. Full points if done in cruisers or nikes. Glad to see I can still bring max ridiculousness even without alcohol. Also might be my first time going full ridiculous since that one thing happened. Probably a good sign.

Starting to feel a bit more like myself, but damn some deep life lessons. This boulder is quite the analogy. I couldn't quite do the natural lowest start on the right hand crimp so I started with right hand already on the arete. I'll be back, or maybe its simply the one that got away. This test piece is located 10 feet to the right of the Reflecting Pool. Start laying down sliding yourself under the boulder as far as possible. No pads are possible, so brace yourself for some rocks in your ass. Wish I could see peoples reactions when they see this rig chalked up.
ascents.zlaggableName: You Don't Get Everything You Want

ascents.comment: Fun yeeting. Yeeted off the pads on one yeet but luckily I’m still invincible.
Waaaaay easier than critically acclaimed. Weird and squeezy like me. Nice consolation prize after missing the one of anything opportunity. Shout out Woo and his beautiful ball sack.

This was nice, good crimps all the way. Group delirium and insanity kicking in. Ladder has changed the game. I didn’t use it here but I forgotten what it’s like jumping to holds you have never touched. Nice send Jaspar and good car ride back. Not enough hack.
If you do this as a YEET it is freaking rad. Group yeeting on this felt good inside. Thanks woo for the slam dunk beta. Jump from the start holds to the sweet as top jug.

Hiking two pads and the ladder out to critically acclaimed was tough. Such a fun hiking adventure. I need a new pad with better straps. Would have flashed if Scott didn’t sabotage me and not tell me where to put my foot. Fun ending to this day. Too ba Drew didn’t have Hulu. Ladder movie screen is plush.

Wowzers. This was a toughie but fun working with Scott, Woo and Rick. Thought this was gonna be a decent crimp warm up for Critically Acclaimed, but after a dozen or so burns I realized it was draining the tank… but never give up! Close on so many different betas but shoutout Rick for finding the jump left betas. Feels more like v8 this way.
I may have heckled Scott a bit too much on this one.

Few goes after doing the stand. Found a finger jab which made it casual. Nothing hard except the not dabbing part. Should probably do it naked so you know if you dabbed or not. Speaking of naked.  Woo is everyone's hero.
cool big holds to kind gross, but not actually gross basically mono pockets. I think as long as temps are decent its cake.

Harder than everything else on this boulder. Wonderful crimp moves to tough top. Top a bit contrived but think I like this better than monkey wrench. Couldn't quite pull Orange Top before driving back to SD but so that's a wrap. Amazing trip. Gregor out.
basically lead with the feet on this one. Heel toe cam followed by heel toe cam followed by heel toe cam. I don't even think you need hand. Fun climbing with my son, Jasper.

This 100% deserves the upgrade. It is an incredible line with amazing features, good movement and good rock quality. If this was in danger of being soft it would be done way more. So upgrade it and get more people on it. It was cold out...ish, but this was baking in the sun. What an inopportune angle. Close on Man is the Beezy! Amazing day out with Woo and Drew, the hike was absolutely miserable. Maybe it was the altitude, maybe it was the snow, maybe its my weak ass, maybe its the two pads ladder and floodies.

So delicate and so wild at the same time. Unless of course you have alien wrists like Woo and can use that pinch prematurely. Temps were primo for this today. Had a moooosive swing on the send. Barely held. Thanks Kevin for your honesty that I swung too far to even spot. Your presence was all I needed. Speaking of which, nice to meet ya! Also shoutout Drew for his inspiring almost send of the SoCal Royalty project, and also shoutout for his subsequent send of said project. Also shout out SoCal Royalty. Long live. Was rewarded with an immaculacy beautiful sunset on topping out. Definitely not fully healed in the heart department, but moments like this are nice.

WHAT There were good boulders nearby the whole time!? Wow. Finally found these on my last day, but dang I could spend several days in this little crag. There must be a ton of boulder fields like this one all across Thailand. Quite a nice little climb! Start on a sharable half pad crimp rail. With low feet pull on up and left to the Gaston. Use a smeary foot and lunge for the lip for a fairly easy lip encounter. Fantastic rock quality and good movement. A bit on the short side but good nonetheless. Up the hill from Torterra ~3 minutes
AKA Torterra Downclimb. So amazing to have a root ladder to go up and down the boulder. So so sick.

Holy wow. The first boulder they showed me was this BEHEMOTH. This boy is a 25 feet boulder with a Ficus tree growing at the top. This is incredible lucky as the Ficus roots entangle and flow down the side to create a perfect root ladder for the downclimb. Anyway this climb starts on the downhill right side sit squat starting on an obvious crimp. a slightly powerful starting sequence leads to some beautifully sculpted in-cuts which make good pause half way up. Then it gets real and slabby. The crux is a super high step like 16 feed off the deck and with terrible hand holds. Pads would have been nice. Pa found me some rope back at the house and it was enough assistance to comfortably suss the crux before pulling from the FA from the ground. Such an incredible memory to leave Thailand with.

Shoutout Gor aka Pa aka my brothers new father in law. He showed me these rocks and even brought me a rope to help suss "Druidcraft". Start on undercling and make a hard left hand cross to a good gaston.
There is an obvious slab on the uphill side of the Torterra boulder. Would be cool to do this direct, but its way easier to bail left to the rail/shelf. Ap would be an amazing climber, wow.

Start as for East Easy Rider but instead follow the logic of "Tim's Fred Traverse".  Could be called "One move into Tim's Fred Traverse". Magical. Actually pretty fun when its not melting here. I met some amazing people this weekend and this boulder is my first memory with them all. Shoutout Lisa, Kelsey, John, Rufio, Davis, Nacho and Echo. John got me on Goldfish Stand and that thing is rad. Will be back. Hopefully I can crimp hard enough for the ending.

Either hard 7 or soft 8 except its obviously not V7 bc it would be done more. Probably V6 / V7 moves into a really hard (and reachy) V5.  Mr. Girth I disagree with your assessment. To be fair I'm still quite fat from my Thailand trip so maybe I'm in the wrong. Fun movement and definitely worth doing. I was able to repeat High Plains first go which rather surprised me. Slightly snowy downclimb, ran up my ladder to help Andrew crux the downclimb. Michelle meeting us out here and convincing me to do a lap on Iron Man, god its been years. Those holds are waaay bigger than I remember. Very fun. Oh also this weekend was magical. Whether the storm scared people off, or people like football more than climbing, bishop was NOT crowded. There was only 5 cars at the milks at the peak. So gorgeous out here with a fresh crop of snow and basically all to ourselves. Now off to Lisa's BDay party! Then dance party?

Has anyone sent this who hasn't climbed V11!? Long live the sandbag, Huzzah! Incredible climb with crazy crux. Was scared I wouldn't have it in me with the extra lbs and third day on, but surprised myself with a quick bag. Awesome climbing this with the crew and the like 20 pads we had. For the big move I slap to the directional sloper not the incut gaston.

Absolutely not V6 wow. I thought this was V8 until I saw the book. Some kinda gross holds, but movement was nice. Hero swing at the top for style pointzzz. We have the Sads to ourselves today, delightful!

Beautiful face that is gross. Enjoyed the hell out of it!  This weekend was amazing, I didn't expect so many wonderful people and memories but I feel like this weekend refilled my soul, thank to all the people who helped fill me up. Big shout out to Lisa and Happy Birthday! Amazing sunset, improbably send, god bishop is beautiful. I love the dramatic emotion change on my face when I stick the lip on this boy. Thanks Kelsey for capturing.

I find grading things at Woodson to be one of the most difficult things ever. Le sigh. Apparently the crack gaston is part of the original beta, which is nice bc it avoids needing to do the last dynamic lunge for which this climb is know. That being said, I totally off routed the big jug (I know I'm so cool) and used the crack to top out directly above the crack. Had a tenuous sequence in the crack but not too hard. I rad like 7 laps on the OG, could probably do blindfolded, and this is definitely harder by a goood degree.

Slightly harder than the OG shield start but fun and worth doing if you find yourself at this boulder too many times. Sit start about 7 feet left of the shield jug matched on a positive crimpy / undeclingy-ish hold. Move up and left to a a hold normally used as a foot on the OG then make a slap to join the OG. Awesome Day at Woodson climbing with new friends. Good conditions and good psyche and camraderie made this a very memorable Woodson day. I reaaaally hope the poison oak outbreak is no too bad... its too much to wish for no rashes but minimal please!

Wow. I cannot believe I did this thing. Keep thinking I'm weak then somehow I do things I didn't think I could do. I have never been able to stick the crux move of this in isolation before.. like not even close so it was a pleasant surprise when it felt good today! Condies were pretty good and group psyche was high. Thanks Aidan for inviting me out today it was an absolute blast. Aidan was SO close on Fake Eppy, and after being inspired by Marcel I decided to barefoot send Fake Eppulator, which was surprisingly easy. I think that's my hardest barefoot send to date!

PRNF: Also 10 Billion Percent been done before. This name is apt bc shoutout camraderie, and also people always shit near eppulator adding their own piles of lore. Perry with the vision, this thing is super fun and will likely do this every time in the Eppy Area. Start on the blocky hold and after gaining the slotty gaston cross left hand to the right and do a short lip traverse / pop to the right facing jug with air underneath you. Mantle up! So fun!

PRNF: 10 Billion Percent been done before but not on MP and quite enjoyable. The trailside corner of the rock leaning on the Eppulator boulder (or the boulder just past Fake Eppuulator) has a large flat blocky jug on the coprner. Start on said jug and make a crux right hand move into a slottty gaston. Once you get the foot up its cake to go straight up.

PRNF: More like class 4 but very enjoyable and pretty. The face texture is unreal if only this was slightly overhung or something. Another great eppy area warm up I should have already done. Thanks Marcel for the rec

This thing is nuts. NUTS I tell you. Way cooler that I envisioned in my head. Than goodness for cloud cover and Eric's unending psyche which is the only reason I tried this today. Crux was crazy for me. I got that high foot then locked off past my shoulder, until I was pushing on the tips of my fully extended fingers. May have to do again for footy bc this was cool.
Somehow I had never done this.

Send train with John! Choo Choo!! Stoked that you waited for me to be back in bishop to make this send train possible. I remember looking at this years and years and years ago and saying like Donkey, "EW! who would want to climb a rock like that!?", this time also like Donkey I said "That is a nice boulder. I like that boulder". Traverses are silly, eliminants are redonk: this is both! But its still fun. GOod shoulder moves, good tension, a big ol jump and another good jump to finish sucker punch.

AKA Squozimodo Left. Bubba Marmaduke Vasko, the legendary black beast, the handsomest good boy, the dog incarnation of a Goron, the water loving ludicrous log fetcher, the "If I spoke my voice would be Morgan Freeman", the grand patriarch and honey badger of a dog... this magnificent furry friend left us today... right around when I sent this climb. Shoutout to all our furry friends who bring so much joy and love into our lives. Special shoutout to Bodhi who also left us a few days ago, another special family member of my sister, Richard and her kids. A goodest boy with the most beautiful dichromatic eyes and majestic coat. Its so hard when we have to say goodbye, but don't worry bc All Dogs Go To Heaven... This climb starts in the same place as Squozimodo but instead of following the natural compression cut left with some cool moves into the jug crack system. For anyone who does this please send a thought out to all the beautiful loving puppos, nekos and all other furry friends in the world.
I always thought this was hard. Turns out its soft.

I think this climb is amazing, been inspired by it for years and so stoke to finally put her down. My send burn was sweet bc I unconsciously pumped myself up for the jump literally saying "Okay, Come on Baby!", thank goodness for footy or the world would never know that. I also said "No fucking way" after sticking it which sums up my experience on this climb and today in general actually. Black mountain day dreaming to the max. Literally did more hard climbs in this single day at Black than I have done in my entire career up to this point (57 climbing days at Black!). So surreal. The world is a simulation and I'm Neo. Before today I had 3 V9s and 3 V10s, after today I have 7 V9s and 5 V10s! What!? Sorry for shoving my psyche down your eyeballs, but well shouting to the 8a ether feels good right now. I also think that its one of those "threshold" climbs where once you have sufficient strength in the right areas (pass the threshold) it feels soft. Its not a very tricky climb. One dead point to a huge incut then a huge move to a jug from said incut.  But it is a test piece for contact strength, essentially a board climb. I suck at board climbing so this was a big milestone for me.

This was the hardest climb I did today hands down. It deserves the upgrade my dudes and dames. Absolutely harder than cosmos. Although.... I realized the way I did it was super fucked up. Getting home I realized the classic beta is the big left hand move to the pocket. I did the normal first move of cosmos, then full spanned right hand to the pocket doing a desperate heel perch where my left hand desperately slides on nothing until I'm actually perched. Once perched in do a big ol' cross to the fin, pausing briefly on the dimple. Also this climb is reachy. Still decently cool, but hard. Shout out send kisses from Kodi!!!

Man the cave through this rock is such a cool formation! That gives this climb an extra star all on its own for novelty. Unfortunately, that about all it gets. Short with okay movement, starting on Jugs is sweet though, so is ending on Jugs. The distance from jug to jug is probably like 6 feet or less which is crazy. AMAZING solo day out here with the mountain all to myself (except that one couple who was hiking.. so no other climbers anyway). Shout out Kodi (not the black mountain pup, but Kodiak the snow loving pup!) for being my climbing partner today and being the soul witness of my best climbing day EVER. I was able to slap from the staring jugs to that sloper, completely skipping the classic gaston sooooo maybe I cheated. Certainly easier if taller. Its my first time being in charge of a dog at the crag and you have so much responsibility! You have to carry poop water and food!? Normally I bring like 2 SpinDrifts for myself but I brought 4 whole liters of water just for the pup, and she drank it all! She's worth it though

Teeechhhnically I did Poop Shoot years ago so I think I may have touched one of these holds before... hopefully the flash police are don't find me in my sleep. Man, double padding with a ladder from the Gate is quite a work out. I am now addicted to ladder unfortunately. Fortunately I'm still Mr Gregor Recian-God so I can handle it. I think I waited just long enough in the day for shade and temps bc this bad boy felt nice. Was worried 2 pads would be too few, but it was fiiiiine. Big moves to big holds, quite and aesthetic and enjoyable climb. Kodi dug a hole and sacked out hard, didn't want to wake her so I set an alarm and took a nap too. Also RIP tree... pretty sure its dead so the hardest part of the climb as per Mr Mathew is gone so must be soft. Kodi loves snow so much. Seeing her rub her nose and slide on every pile was so cute. Fill my cup with cuteness little girl.

It's crazy when weather likes to be pristine on the weekdays and terrible on weekends. Thank god I have a job where I can simply transmute a weekday into a weekend when need be. I love that there are still good FAs visible from the road at black. This thing is sweet. Was really hoping to follow in my boy Aden's footsteps but the flash eluded me. I think MAYBE if I waited for temps on this one it might have gone, but that wide pinch was harder to grab right than I thought. A few susses on getting the right heel up then it went smooth as Leo's bottom. I squeeze professionally so as soon as I was through that crux nothing was going to get me off.. except this climb.. which it did 😉

Exit the uphill side of the Hall of the Mountain King and go right (east). Follow the boulder on your right hand side like 20 feet to the end of a decomposing fell tree. There you will find a cool crimp at head height. Pull onto said crimp, and use crumbling nothing feet for a near campus to a grainy sloper, then do one more thrutch with equally bad feet to a jug. The quality of the starting crimp makes this climb worth doing. I would not be surprised if Kody has already done this. Also could be V5 or V6 but grades are very hard to discern at the moment.
ascents.zlaggableName: Hall Pass for a Grecian God

ascents.comment: Simply one of the best there is. Looks great and climbs even better. I'm still slightly ill with the flu or a cold and still sent this in just a handful of goes. This is absolutely my style, temps were crisp and I'm climbing better than I ever have, but I think V9 is more appropriate. I've done a bunch in the 9/10 range last week and this seems on par with Squozimoto, personally slightly easier. Grades are funny though bc I think Man Is The Bastard is harder than this by a good margin (although I'm sure many would disagree). Drew is that "LEGIT SAVAGE" and will level up to unlock the low!! you got this my dude! Great day climbing with you and the mountain to ourselves.
ascents.zlaggableName: In the Hall of the Mountain King Part 2

ascents.comment: Words will not convey the craziness that was today. It snowed 8+ inches yesterday, I did not realize this was going to be the case. I thought maybe 2. Black Mountain was truly a winter wonderland today. You literally could have snowboarded down the road. The trees were all plastered with snow. A first for me to see trees rouse and slowly shake off all the fresh snow from the day before. 24 hours ago there was no snow on the trees, at the start of the day they were plastered, at the end of the day they once again had nothing. To be bathing in sunlight while watching snow fall all around you, the sounds of water and snow plopping all around you. So crazy.
